title: Guard plugin-extension registry setup behind login check
answers: Why is /metas called on the login screen?
How to avoid unnecessary plugin registry API calls for anonymous users
Unnecessary network call on Grafana login page
body:
Symptom: Grafana called the plugin-extension registries setup (hitting /metas) even on the login screen before a user was authenticated.
Root cause: AppWrapper.tsx called getPluginExtensionRegistries() unconditionally on mount, and app.ts also called it a second time redundantly.
Fix pattern: gate any call that needs a logged-in user behind `contextSrv.user.orgRole !== ''`, and keep only one call site; initialize state with a safe default (`initRegistries([])`) so the provider always has a value even when the guarded call is skipped.
Constraints: applies to initialization code that depends on an authenticated user (orgRole set); do not apply this guard to code paths required for anonymous/public access (public dashboards, snapshots).
applies: public/app/AppWrapper.tsx and public/app/app.ts plugin-extension registry initialization
says: Why is plugin registry initialized before I log in?
Stop fetching plugin extensions when user isn't authenticated yet
Avoid unnecessary network requests on the login screen
Plugin registry loading happens too early in startup
search: Plugin-extension registry setup calls must be guarded by a login check because the registries endpoint requires an authenticated user, yet AppWrapper and app.ts were calling it unconditionally even on the login screen. Gate calls to getPluginExtensionRegistries() behind `contextSrv.user.orgRole !== ''`, keep only one initialization call site, and initialize provider state with a safe default (initRegistries([])) so it always has a value when the guarded call is skipped. Do not apply this guard to code paths required for public/anonymous access like public dashboards or snapshots. Applies to public/app/AppWrapper.tsx and public/app/app.ts initialization of plugin-extension registries in public/app/features/plugins/extensions/registry/setup.ts.
